articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 4
articles.meta: Thu 27th August 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Another week, another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. And then there were three in the FA Cup

The Emirates FA Cup Preliminary Round was the key feature of the weekend for a total of nine NWCFL sides. Of those nine, three now remain in English Football’s Oldest Cup Competition.

South Liverpool slipped past fellow NWCFL outfit Longridge Town 3-2 away from home; Prestwich Heys overcame stiff resistance from last season’s First Division South runaway champions Runcorn Town on the road, winning 3-1; and Trafford survived a late fightback by Runcorn Linnets to win 3-2, and complete a hat-trick of away victories for the remaining NWCFL sides in the competition.

2. Burscough the team to beat in the Prem?

On Saturday, the Linnets became the first team in the Premier Division this season to record a double-digit points tally - albeit, they have played the joint most league games at this time. To say that they don’t deserve to top the table as we approach September, however, might be blasphemous.

After slowing down over the course of the prior week, Saturday saw Phil Stafford’s team return to their best as they emerged victorious over Abbey Hey in a 6-3 barnstormer of a game, which featured a hat-trick of penalty goals for Callum Laird. You’ve got to win ‘em to score ‘em, and Burscough certainly did that this past weekend.

3. The wait goes on for AFC Liverpool

At the other end of the Premier Division table right now are AFC Liverpool. Last season’s Macron Cup winners knew that 2026/27 would come with an adjustment period after the departure of their long-time gaffer and core squad in the summer, but few could’ve foreseen seven straight defeats in all competitions to begin the campaign.

And yet, here we are. AFC Liverpool are currently propping up the Prem, and they are the only remaining team across the NWCFL who are yet to score a point. They face promotion-battle veterans Ramsbottom United on bank holiday weekend, who were shellshocked by a late Atherton LR comeback last time out – maybe AFC can catch them off guard this Saturday.

4. Maghull lay down the baton

At the time of writing, there are three points separating first from seventh in the Prem, with a fluctuating number of games played by all teams involved – expected early-season uncertainty, then. In the South, just one point separates table-toppers AFC Bridgnorth from sixth placed Sandbach United, with the leaders currently holding a single game in hand on the chasing pack.

Maghull – top of the tree in the First Division North – have no such worries. Seven games into the new campaign, Joe Burns’ side have been nearly perfect, save for an opening day defeat by Darwen FC. They have a three-point headstart on second-placed Thornton Cleveleys at this stage, and a further two points on the next three teams down. It’s early days, but Maghull look like the NWCFL’s most prominent pacesetters right now.

5. GTF In at Widnes Town

A poor start to their maiden season as an NWCFL side has hopefully dropped to its lowest point for Widnes Town after their 7-0 defeat to Allscott Heath on Saturday. In order to turn their fortunes around, the First Division South’s bottom side have opted for a managerial change.

Paul McNally has left the club, and his replacement brings quite a bit of name value with him. This week, the club have appointed local cult hero Gary Taylor-Fletcher as manager. Taylor-Fletcher played for Blackpool and Leicester City in his pro career, and he scored the Seasiders’ first ever Premier League goal. He will hope to bring the same attacking threat he possessed as a player to the Chemics.

articles.title: Lorraine Beavers Visits Thornton Cleveleys
articles.meta: Wed 26th August 2026 | Thornton Cleveleys | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Lorraine Beavers, Labour for Blackpool North and Fleetwood, visited Gamble Road to find out more about developments at Thornton Cleveleys and met with club chairman Steve Abbott.

The fact-finding mission centred on the work of the club around community involvement, juniors setup, senior and women's football. Along with developments on, and off, the pitch.

Mrs Beavers was shown around the club facilities including the Salthouse Bar which has just had planning permission for an extension to the room size.

The Member of Parliament for for Blackpool North and Fleetwood was pleased with her introduction to the club.

"I'd just like to say it's amazing, the community must love this area as you've done so much. I can't believe how many pitches you have and the work you do in the community.  I think this area of Thornton is very lucky to have you here.

"It's been a real inspiration to talk people who care for the community and the club itself. I can't wait to visit again. Thank you very much for inviting me today."

Chairman Steve Abbott thanked the MP for visiting.

"It was a great today to have a catchup with Lorraine Beavers, our local MP.   It was good that she made the time to come along and have a look round. She was very impressed with what we are doing for the local community and how many children and adults we have involved with the club.  We also spoke about our journey into supporting disability football at the club.

"Lorraine was very happy with our impact on the local area and is happy to work with us on future projects. It was a very worthwhile visit. She was impressed with what we are doing for the local area including Thornton-Cleveleys and Fleetwood. Hopefully, our relationship will long continue."

articles.title: Emirates FA Cup First Qualifying Round
articles.meta: Mon 24th August 2026 | FA Competition News | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The FA have today released the draws for the First Qualifying Round of the Emirates FA Cup.

Of the 19 Premier Division clubs that entered the Emirates FA Cup this season, we are down to just four, with three winning last Saturday and one requiring a midweek replay if they are to join them.

South Liverpool and Prestwich Heys were two of the sides winning on Saturday, and they have been drawn against each other in the First Qualifying Round. South have played just four times this season but have won three and drew one of them. Prestwich have played six times, and after losing their opening day match, are unbeaten in the last five games with three wins and two draws.

They haven't played each other this season yet, but the league game is scheduled just seven days after this cup tie! The draw does mean one of our sides are guaranteed a place in the Second Qualifying Round, but we'd rather they play others so that they could both progress!

Trafford's reward for winning at Runcorn Linnets will be an away trip to another Northern Premier League side, this time travelling to NPL Premier Division side Bamber Bridge. The Preston side have won just one of their opening five league games, and enter the FA Cup at this stage.

It's the first time in nine years that Bamber Bridge have played one of our sides in the FA Cup, although they lost that 2017 clash as Ashton Athletic beat them 2-1.

Litherland REMYCA face a midweek replay at Prescot Cables. Should they win that then they will be at home to with NPL West side 1874 Northwich or Northern League side Horbury Town.

1874 are no strangers to our sides having played in the NWCFL for plenty of years before being laterally moved to the Midland League. They achieved promotion from that league last season via the play-off's and have started the season with a win, a draw and a loss, with a win and draw in the FA Cup.

Horbury Town play in the Northern Counties East and have played just three league games with two wins and a draw. Their only loss from seven games this season came in the FA Vase last weekend.

Horbury have never faced one of our sides in the FA Cup, but have played twice in the FA Vase, both of those games going to penalties.

Ties will be played on Saturday 5th September 2026.

The draw including our sides can be found below:

SATURDAY 8 AUGUST 2026

WINNERS RECEIVE £2,250

LOSERS RECEIVE £750

1. Bamber Bridge v Trafford

2. Litherland REMYCA or Prescot Cables v 1874 Northwich or Horbury Town

articles.title: Week 3: Summary
articles.meta: Sat 22nd August 2026 | Match Reviews | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
EMIRATES FA CUP PRELIMINARY ROUND

South Liverpool are through to the First Qualifying Round of the FA Cup for the first time since 1990 after a 3-2 win at Longridge Town. Two goals from Jack Bentley, either side of one from George Clarkson, put them into a three goal lead midway through the second half. Goals from Francis Leather and Ethan Gough made for a tense finale but South held on to progress.

Trafford produced a giant killing with a 3-2 win at NPL side Runcorn Linnets. Ryan Brooke - Linnets' all time leading scorer - and Jensen Bowering put Trafford two ahead at the break David Worrall adding a third at the start of the second half. Linnets reduced the arrears before adding another in stoppage time, but could not find an equaliser.

Prestwich Heys are also through after a fine away win, that a 3-1 victory at Runcorn Town. After a goalless first half, Ellis Richardson and Tobias Green put Heys two goals ahead with Runcorn reducing the arrears with 20 minutes remaining. Matthew Smyth restored the two goal lead to see Heys through.

Litherland REMYCA live to fight another day after a 1-1 draw with NPL side Prescot Cables. Both goals came in first half stoppage time with Prescot going ahead before REMY equalised. The replay is midweek.

Elsewhere Droylsden levelled against Garforth Town with ten minutes remaining before losing 2-1 to a last minute winner. Nelson went down to a narrow 1-0 loss at Witton Albion.

The final game saw Euxton Villa bow out after a 3-2 loss at Lower Breck.

PREMIER DIVISION .

Atherton LR left it late to record a 2-1 victory at home to Ramsbottom United. An own goal midway through the first half put Rammy ahead with Cal Hunter levelling with five minutes to go. Hunter then netted the winner two minutes into stoppage time.

Burscough romped to a 6-3 victory at home to Abbey Hey with Callum Laird grabbing a hattrick for the Linnets. Jordan Darr scored twice for Charnock Richard as they won 3-0 at home to AFC Liverpool.

Glossop North End won 1-0 at home to Chadderton, with the final game finishing goalless between Barnoldswick Town and FC St Helens.

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

Maghull made it six successive wins with a 3-0 win at Garstang. Connor Rankin put them ahead just after the half hour with Jamie Clark adding another from the penalty spot six minutes into the second half. Nathan Peetwon secured the win with the third ten minutes from time.

Ashton Town also ran out 3-0 winners at Maine Road, all the goals there coming in the first half. However the biggest win of the day was from Steeton who won 4-0 at Squires Gate. Joshua Coe and Kevin Gonzalez put them two ahead inside 17 minutes, before adding another two in the second half.

Jacob Ngoy scored twice for Flixton as they beat AFC Blackpool 3-1 at home. Colne were 3-0 winners at home to Uppermill, all the goals there coming in the second half.

Cammell Laird 1907 also scored three as they beat Fulwood Amateurs 3-2. Ben Wood scored twice for Lairds, with Spencer Lucas also scoring two for the visitors.

Jacob Aspinall was another two score twice for Thornton Cleveleys as they won 2-1 at Ashton Athletic. Woolton won by the same scoreline at Daisy Hill, with Ashville being the third side of the day to win 2-1, their winner from Jack Edwards coming in stoppage time.

Bacup Borough drew 1-1 at home to AFC Knowsley, with Holker Old Boys' game with Halewood Apollo also finishing with that scoreline.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

The biggest win of the season so far came from Allscott Heath as they beat Widnes Town 7-0. There were six different scorers with Benjamin Summers netting a brace with the opening two goals of the game.

There was a remarkable finale to the game at New Mills where Shawbury United led 2-1 deep into stoppage time. Six minutes into added time, Cameron Tetlow levelled for the Millers before Luc Ferry hit the winner for the home side a minute later.

Sam Preece scored twice for AFC Bridgnorth as they won 3-2 away at Alsager Town, that result moving them to the top of a tight league table, with Callum Parker scoring twice for Stafford Town in their 3-0 home win against Crewe.

Sandbach United cruised to a 4-1 home win over hitheroe leaders Wolverhampton Casuals. Dawley Town won 3-1 at home to Market Drayton Town, with Cheadle Heath Nomads winning 1-0 at Wednesfield Community thanks to Chigozie Ewelike's stoppage time winner.

Eccleshall won 1-0 at Foley Meir, with Bilston Town drawing 1-1 at home with Barnton. The final game saw Rhyce Brown sciore twice for Telford Town, but they were held 2-2 thanks to Samuel Mellor's leveller seven minutes into stoppage time.

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 3
articles.meta: Thu 20th August 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Another week, another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. The Isuzu FA Vase is back!

Like the week prior, this past Saturday was dominated by a nationwide domestic cup competition. The FA Vase returned for 2026/27, and 31 NWCFL made their bows in the first qualifying round.

Of those 31, 11 won their matches outright with choice cuts including Eccleshall hammering Allscott Heath 4-0 at home; First Division South side Barnton upsetting the odds in a 3-1 away win against Premier Division Irlam; and Charnock Richard, Atherton LR, Foley Meir and Telford Town all winning in a dreaded penalty shootout.

2. Gate open for the second qualifier

One team that did’nt feature in the weekend’s FA Vase fixture list, despite initially being scheduled to do so, were First Division North outfit Squires Gate. The seaside club were due to welcome Northern Football League side Boro Rangers, but instead, were given a bye into the next round.

The reason for this goes back to early July, when Boro Rangers folded its senior men’s team after, in their own words, “financial and operational challenges made the team unsustainable.” It’s real a shame that this sort of thing continues to happen up and down the football pyramid, especially given how much money there is in football currently. There’s a slim positive in all this for Gate, however, who were automatically granted a place in the second Vase qualifier.

3. Barnoldswick Town know the draw

Barlick are three league games into the new season, and are currently undefeated, which sounds great. Then you look deeper, and you’ll see that they are also winless, and 13th in the table.

Every NWCFL game that Gerry Harrison and Lewis Craig’s men have played thus far has ended honours even. Away at Abbey Hey on the opening day, it finished 2-2; away at Prestwich Heys in their first midweek game of the season, it finished 1-1; and at home to Ramsbottom United on Tuesday, it also finished 1-1. They even drew their FA Cup EP round tie with Atherton Collieries 12 days ago, only to be beaten in the replay.

4. Hard times for Ashton Town

The season so far has been nothing short of a struggle for Ashton Town. Last season, they were one of many contenders for the title around the festive period, but from their opening six league games this time around, they are yet to get on the board.

They have played the joint-most league games of any side in the First Division North in 2026/27 at the time of writing, alongside Maghull and Holker Old Boys, but haven’t been able to record a win or draw in any of them. Their next fixture sees them travel to face Maine Road - seventh time’s the charm?

5. AFC Bridgnorth too bold to beat

Currently second in the First Division South table, and with a game in hand on early leaders Wolverhampton Casuals, AFC Bridgnorth are thriving in their maiden NWCFL campaign. The WV16 side have recorded three wins and a draw in their first four matches, taking 10 points from an available 12.

It doesn’t take a mathematician to work out that they are yet to suffer a league defeat this season, which is impressive on its own, but they are also the only remaining side in the First Division South not to have given up all the points in a league game this season. It will interesting to see who can slay the dragon.

articles.title: Week 3: Manager Quotes
articles.meta: Mon 17th August 2026 | Manager Reactions | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Isuzu FA Vase:

This past weekend saw the return of the Isuzu FA Vase, with a total of 31 NWCFL sides making their competition bow on Saturday. Of those sides, 11 progressed to the next round, including Premier Division Atherton LR on penalties after a 2-2 draw with First Division North side Cammell Laird 1907.

Following such a tense victory, manager Dave Jones said: "I thought we put in a really good performance on and off the ball for 55 minutes. Once they got a goal out of nothing, the picture just changed slightly and gave them something to go after.

"It’s about finding a way to win in cup games and we done that. Full credit to Cammell Laird - I thought they were organised and played really well, and they pushed us all the way. We need to kick on now, rest up and go again on Tuesday at home to Chadderton."

Another Premier Division side that came out on top in a Vase outing on Saturday were Trafford. They put Armthorpe Welfare to the sword in a 4-0 away victory, after which manager Tom Baker said: "We're pleased to get into the next round - that was the main objective.

"It's always difficult having two coach journeys over the space of six days. We played against a really good side, who are at the top of their league, and they've had a really good start. We knew the game was going to be difficult, and that we were going to have to apply ourselves properly, but I felt that if we did that, we were going to win the game.

"Being honest, I wasn't happy with the first half performance - I thought we were ambling through the first 45. We got out noses in front, but I felt like we were making it a contest, but if we had put our foot on the gas, we could have got a few goals in the first half.

"I think it took us probably 10 minutes in the second half to find our groove, but then for the next 30 or 35 minutes, we were the dominant team. We started to do the basics really well, which allowed us to create space, and then we showed some real quality in the goals that we scored."

FC St Helens also guaranteed their place in the next round after their 2-0 victory away from home against Ashton Athletic. Following the result, manager Mike Smith said: "It was a performance that started with a little bit of nerves.

"But we grew into the game and settled down once we scored the first goal. Our second half performance was really good, and we played the majority of it in Ashton Athletic's half of the pitch.

"It was controlled performance and a good, much-needed win."

Finally from the Vase, in something of an upset, First Division South side Barnton knocked of Premier Division Irlam to secure their place in the hat for the next round. Following the whistle, manager Lewis Wood called it a "huge result for the lads!

"A massive win for us against Irlam, who are a strong team and a league above us. The boys showed incredible character, effort and belief from start to finish.

"Credit to every player and every member of the club who was involved. We’ve shown exactly what it means to be a Villager this weekend. What a performance. What a result!"

Premier Division:

Away from the cup contests of the weekend, there was a handful of league action to speak of, including at the home of Chadderton. They welcome Nelson to the Emplas Commercial North Stadium, and saw them off with a 2-1 win, after which, joint-manager Ben Greenidge said: "We went into the game Saturday off the back of two very good midweek training sessions.

"We knew the threat Nelson had in targeting their big man up top, and the boys handled him very well. We needed a fast start and we got exactly that; a great goal in the first couple of minutes finished off by the returning Lazenbury. We weathered a load of corners against us in the first half and went in at half time 1-0 up.

"In the second half, we asked questions of their defence by putting it on them from throw-ins etc, and that's where our second goal came from. A great finish from captain Luke!

"An unforced error with 10 minutes to go gave them a penalty, which Ollie saved tremendously, put they reacted quickest, scoring from the rebound. It made the last five minutes of the game a bit nervy, when we should have been seeing the game out comfortably at 2-0, but we got the three points. Now, it's onto Tuesday away at Atherton LR."

First Division North:

Also in league action were Garstang, in the First Division North. Aided by a Weslie Bajraliu hat-trick, they recorded a 3-0 home win over divisional newcomers AFC Knowsley. After full-time, gaffer Guy Heffernan said: "First of all, it’s great to get on the board, and gain some points - but we should have scored more!

"We missed a penalty, and missed some guilt-edge chances that we should have punished AFC Knowsley for. Fair play to our visitors - they never stopped, and they have some decent players.

"But overall, it's a massive three points for us, but we need to find some consistency now, and keep gaining points going forward."

articles.title: Week 3: Summary
articles.meta: Sun 16th August 2026 | Match Reviews | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
ISUZU FA VASE FIRST QUALIFYING ROUND

Trafford's first FA Vase tie since 2007 saw them cruise into the next round after a 3-0 win at Armthorpe Welfare. Bile Ahmed put them ahead on the stoke of half time and added the third in the final minute, with Kyle Worsley getting the other for Trafford midway through the half.

Dudley Town are also through after a 3-0 win over Alsager Town, but the biggest win of the day belonged to Eccleshall who beat Allscott Heath 4-0.

First Division South side Barnton pulled off a shock as they won 2-1 away at Premier Division side Irlam. Another win against a higher side came as First Division North side Colne won 2-1 at Premier Division Barnoldswick Town.

FC St Helens are safely through after a 2-0 win at Ashton Athletic with Darwen also pulled off a fine away win as they won 2-1 at NCEL side Winterton Rangers. A big away win saw Litherland REMYCA win 4-1 at Maine Road, Cameron Taylor scoring twice for Remy.

Five games went to penalties with four of our sides progressing. First Division South side Telford Town beat Midland Premier side Darlaston Town 6-5 from the spit after a 1-1 draw, with Foley Meir winning 4-2 on penalties after a goalless draw with Redditch Borough.

Atherton LR surrendered a two goal lead to draw 2-2 with Cammell Laird 1907 but won 3-1 from the spot, whilst Charnock Richard drew 1-1 at Appleby Frodingham before winning 4-3 on penalties.

The only side not to progress were Euxton Villa, who conceded in stoppage time to draw 2-2 at Retford before losing 6-5 from the spot.

Abbey Hulton United won 3-0 at Stafford Town with Wythenshawe Town winning by the same scoreline at Cheadle Heath Nomads. Wednesfield Community went down 4-1 at home to Sutton United, with Studley beating Market Drayton Town 3-1. Northwich Victoria were 2-0 winners at New Mills.

Former NWCFL side Kendal Town beat Steeton 2-1, with Flixton losing their first Vase game since reformation as they lost 4-2 at home to Worsborough Bridge Athletic. Two time finalists Glossop North End went down 2-0 at home to Staveley Miners Welfare, with Boldon Community Association beating Longridge Town 2-1.

PREMIER DIVISION .

There were just three games in the Premier Division this afternoon with Burscough's 100% winning start coming to an end with a 2-1 home defeat by Droylsden..Cody Artwell and Jordan Barnet scored either side of half time for the Bloods, with Deacon Smalley grabbing a consolation in stoppage time.

It was the same scoreline at Chadderton who beat Nelson 2-1, with the other game ending 1-1 between Abbey Hey and Prestwich Heys, both goals there coming in the first half.

There is one more Premier Division game of the day as FC Isle of Man host Ramsbottom United. .

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

Garstang won their first game of the season with a 3-0 win at home to AFC Knowsley. After five successive losses, it was a hat-trick from Weslie Bajraliu that proved the difference.

Brandon Collins grabbed a brace for Holker Old Boys as they beat Ashton Town 3-0, with Nathan Salisbury also scoring twice for Halewood Apollo in their 4-2 win at Thornton Cleveleys.

Spencer Lucas hit two for Fulwood Amateurs as they won 4-1 at Ashville, with Maghull coming from behind to win 2-1 at Uppermill, a result that moves them top of the table.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

AFC Bridgnorth made it three wins from four games as they came from behind to beat Crewe 4-1, Nehemia Zazi hitting two late goals for the Shropshire side.

Shawbury United beat Widnes 3-2 in an extraordinary game with all goals coming in the first half, the home side taking the lead at the break after trailing when the added time board went up.

Bilston Town won 3-0 at Brereton Social, whilst Wolverhampton Casuals top the table after a 1-0 win at Dawley Town.

articles.title: Week 3: Preview
articles.meta: Fri 14th August 2026 | Match Previews | By Ben Wilkinson
articles.body:
ISUZU FA VASE - 1st QUALIFYING ROUND

FRIDAY 14TH AUGUST

There are a couple of fixtures on Friday night to open the weekend, including an all-NWCFL tie. Daisy Hill host longtime Counties stalwarts Cheadle Town, who are now members of the Midland League Premier Division and have won one and lost one of their start to life in a new league. The Cutters are yet to taste defeat in normal time this season and despite the difference in Steps between the pair, they will be hoping for an early upset on home turf.

Elsewhere, there’s a Liverpool derby as AFC Liverpool travel to Woolton. It’s four defeats from four for the Non-League Reds so far this term and they are yet to notch in the goals for column, and they’re up against a Woolton side who haven’t lost yet, two wins from their opening two being followed up by a pair of draws as they look to gain promotion at the second time of asking. A win in the Vase could do wonders for confidence for either team as they look set to battle at opposing ends of the league tables.

SATURDAY 15TH AUGUST

Appleby Frodingham vs Charnock Richard

Charnock Richard arrive in Lincolnshire after a mixed start to the season, with a win, a draw and a loss in their opening three encounters. They were dumped out of the Emirates FA Cup by Litherland REMYCA last weekend so are out to avoid a double early exit, and stand a good chance against Step 6 opposition on Saturday afternoon. Appleby Frodingham, known as the Steelmen, currently sit rock bottom of the Northern Counties East Division One, having lost all four of their league games to date with a goal difference of -14. This isn’t the Steelmen’s first rodeo against an NWCFL team as Nelson beat them 3-2 at this stage of the competition way back in 2012/13 - in fact, they are yet to win a game in the FA Vase at all!

Armthorpe Welfare vs Trafford

Trafford follow up on their successful outing over the Pennines last weekend with another trip east, this time to Doncaster to take on Armthorpe Welfare. Wellie, as their are affectionately known by their supporters, are sitting pretty at the top of the NCEL Division One, with 10 points from their opening four games. Trafford may well see themselves as favourites still but it doesn’t look like it will be an easy game.

Ashton Athletic vs FC St Helens

FC St Helens look to kickstart their season in a local derby away at Ashton Athletic. The Stripes have lost both league games so far and fell to a late goal in their FA Cup replay at home to North Ferriby during the week. Their opposition aren’t the easiest to break down though, Athletic have kept a clean sheet in three of their four games in all competitions, though the outlier was a 4-0 drubbing at Flixton in the Edward Case Cup last weekend.

Atherton LR vs Cammell Laird 1907

It’s another all-Counties tie at Crilly Park where Cammell Laird visit Atherton LR. Neither side has really got going this season and LR took a battering at the hands of Euxton Villa last time out, conceding six without response. Lairds have fared better, with a 2-1-1 record from their first four league outings, including a topsy-turvy 4-3 win at Flixton, where Adam Smith scored two of his four goals so far this season.

Barnoldswick Town vs Colne

It’s a local derby deep into east Lancashire here where Barnoldswick Town take on Colne. It’s been a couple of years since these two traded blows; Jude Entwistle’s late goal saw Colne take the points in a 3-2 win on Boxing Day 2024, though that season would ultimately result in relegation for the Reds.

Barlick curiously drew their opening hat-trick of games before falling 2-0 in a FA Cup replay against Atherton LR midweek whilst Colne have lost both league games to date, although they did thump Garstang 3-0 in the Edward Case Cup in between.

Boldon CA vs Longridge Town

Longridge have a third successive away trip as they trek up to the North East to face Boldon CA, a side top of the Northern League Division Two with five wins from six. The Ridge will hope to have enough to see off a Step 6 outfit but expect a tight game here with the hosts bang in form.

Cheadle Heath Nomads vs Wythenshawe Town

It’s a South Manchester matchup and a first competitive meeting between these two since February 2020 as Nomads welcome Wythenshawe Town. Town won 5-0 on that day six and a half years ago but it’s all change since then, and despite playing at a Step higher and having just come down from Step 4, Nomads will fancy themselves against their visiting opponents who have yet to get off the mark this term.

Dudley Town vs Alsager Town

Alsager have lost three games on the spin and come up against Step 5 opposition in the form of Dudley Town. The Robins have lost both of their Midland League Premier Division fixtures to date but will eye this fixture up as an opportunity to get their season back on track, whilst the Bullets will have to be at their best to bridge the gap and produce a cupset in the West Midlands.

Eccleshall vs Allscott Heath

Eccleshall have started the season strongly, beating Widnes Town 3-1 on opening day and edging out leaders Wolverhampton Casuals during the week; their only blemish to date being a 2-1 defeat at home to Barnton. It’s an inter-division clash at the Stoke Signage Stadium and it’s basement boys Allscott Heath who come to town, just 11 days after the last meeting between the pair - Eccy winning that one 4-0.

Flixton vs Worsbrough Bridge Athletic

Flixton make their FA Vase debut 16 years after the old club last played in the competition, and their first opponents are Worsborough Bridge Athletic, regular foes with NWCFL clubs in recent years, most recently last weekend when Trafford ran out 2-0 winners! Despite their middling league position, Flixton have been free-scoring so far and having enticed last season’s record-breaking Premier Division top scorer, Lewis-Simon Byrne, to drop a level, he has excelled and scored in every game he has played for the club.

Foley Meir vs Redditch Borough

Foley Meir have blown hot and cold so far, with a LWLW sequence to their name. They will hope to break that streak here against Hellenic League Division One outfit Redditch Borough. Redditch suffered a heavy 8-1 defeat in their first league game and have won one and lost one since then to leave them 14th in their 18-strong Step 6 division.

Kendal Town vs Steeton

Steeton haven’t been far away from goals this season, their four games thus far have produced 17 goals. Early defeats to favourites Daisy Hill and Holker Old boys have been put behind them with home wins against new-boys AFC Knowsley and most recently a 4-2 victory against Bacup Borough during the week. Frontman Joshua Coe is already on four goals for the season and he will be one to watch as the Chevvies travel to Step 5 opposition looking to cause an upset. The Mintcakes have already played six games this season, losing just one of those, an opening day derby defeat at Carlisle City in the Northern League Division One.

New Mills vs Northwich Victoria

New Mills opened their season with a stunning 6-0 win over Telford Town, with Solomon Richards and Luke Evans both scoring twice. Northwich Victoria, of the Step 5 Midland League Premier Division, will be a tougher test, but New Mills’ early form will give them plenty of confidence and belief that they can pull off an unlikely victory.

Retford vs Euxton Villa

Euxton Villa come into this tie with bags of confidence after hammering Atherton LR 6-0 last weekend and face a Retford side who are going well in the NCEL Premier Division, sitting 5th after 4 games. Retford played on Tuesday nugth whilst Villa have had a full week’s rest, that could prove to be pivotal in a game sure to be finely poised.

Route One Rovers vs AFC Blackpool

AFC Blackpool have a tough test against former NWCFL members Route One Rovers. Route Onr won 9-0 (nine) in their league outing last weekend and followed that up with a 5-3 victory in their league cup during the week, so are firing on all fronts and the Mechanics will need to try to curb this scoring spree if they are to harbour hopes of progressing to the next round.

Studley vs Market Drayton Town

Market Drayton got their campaign up and running at the third time of asking, beating Telford Town 1-0 on Tuesday after losing their opening pair. Their opponents and hosts on Saturday, Studley, have had a middling start to their season in the Hellenic League Division One and this could be a close-fought encounter.

Winterton Rangers vs Darwen FC

Darwen have impressed early on after just missing out on the playoffs in the spring, beating Maghull and Uppermill either side of a draw with Woolton. Their opponents on Saturday, Winterton Rangers, have had a mixed start, winning two and losing two of their opening four league games in the NCEL Division One, alongside an exit in the first round of their league cup during the week. It’s Rangers’ first matchup against an NWCFL side since 2022/23, when Prestwich Heys ran out 2-1 winners in the Second Round of this competition.

Other fixtures:

Glossop North End vs Staveley Miners Welfare

Irlam vs Barnton

Maine Road vs Litherland REMYCA

Sandbach United vs Ashby IvanhoeSelby Town vs Bacup Borough

Stafford Town vs Abbey Hulton United

Telford Town vs Darlaston Town

Wednesfield Community vs Sutton United

NWCFL PREMIER DIVISION

SATURDAY 15TH AUGUST

Burscough vs Droylsden

In a fixture curiosity, this will be the THIRD time these two play inside eight days! They followed up a 2-2 draw at Burscough’s Community Ground last weekend with a 3-0 Droylsden win in the replay at the Butchers’ Arms on Tuesday, meaning the visiting Bloods will be full of confidence as they look to inflict the Linnets first dropped points of their league campaign, whilst continuing their own 100% record. Burscough’s Callum Laird has scored in three of their four games whilst Droylsden’s Nellson Van already has two to his name.

Chadderton vs Nelson

Chadderton fell to Witton Albion in the Emirates FA Cup last weekend so their attention reverts back to the league campaign, and following a bright start they will be looking to return to winnings ways against Nelson in the first game between the pair since April 2023, when both were still plying their trade in the First Division North.

FC Isle of Man vs Ramsbottom United (18:00)

The late kick off on the Island sees two sides unbeaten in the league face off against one another. FC Isle of Man have yet to concede in the league, beating FC St Helens and drawing at Glossop North End, whilst Rammy shared the spoils at Litherland before toppling Trafford by scoring three without reply. Gareth Hill has scored a goal in every game so far this season - will he continue that run at The Bowl?

Elsewhere, Abbey Hey host Prestwich Heys.

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

SATURDAY 15TH AUGUST

Garstang vs AFC Knowsley

Garstang have struggled again this term, losing all three league games and being turfed out of the Edward Case Cup at the hands of Colne. A first visit of AFC Knowsley to the Riverside may give them some respite, the newcomers also got off to a losing start before finally getting off the mark by beating Fulwood Amateurs on Tuesday night.

Holker Old Boys vs Ashton Town

Holker aim to make it four wins from five in their bright start to a 27th consecutive FIrst Division (North) campaign. The Stags’ next opponent is an Ashton Town side who’s leaky defence has cost them so far, conceding three in every game so far and falling to defeat on every occasion.

Uppermill v Maghull

Uppermill, using Mossley’s Seel Park as a temporary base whilst their own home is upgraded to Step 6 standards, haven’t had the best start to life in the Counties and have picked up just one point from their opening trio of league games. Maghull travel to east Manchester in fine form, sitting top of the division and with two three-goal victories in succession during the past seven days.

Also in the First Division North, Halewood Apollo go to Thornton Cleveleys and Fulwood Amateurs travel to Ashville’s Ray Parker Stadium.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

SATURDAY 15TH AUGUST

Brereton Social vs Bilston Town

Brereton Social seek to continue their perfect start to life in the NWCFL against another new side in the form of Bilston Town. Both sides won 2-0 on opening day, but Bilston have lost twice to AFC Bridgnorth since then (one cup, one league) whilst Social have gone from strength to strength, knocking off first Alsager Town and then Dawley Town in the cup, both away from home. This marks their first NWCFL home game and another victory here would be the perfect way to mark such a milestone.

Dawley Town vs Wolverhampton Casuals

The Cassies have started superbly in their sophomore NWCFL season, winning their first three without conceding before a 2-1 reverse at home to Eccleshall during the week ended that run. They do still sit top of the tree though and next up for them is a trip to newcomers Dawley Town, who despite scoring 2 goals in every game so far, only have one point (and a cup exit) to their name. Cassies’ Kieran Cook heads up the divisional top scorer table with five goals already.

Elsewhere, AFC Bridgnorth take on Crewe and Widnes Town head south to Shawbury United.

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 2
articles.meta: Thu 13th August 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Another week, another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. The World's Oldest Cup Competition

The FA Cup returned last weekend for 2026/27! All 20 Premier Division sides made their bows across Saturday and Sunday, with eight winning their matches in the Extra-Preliminary round outright, with a ninth, Droylsden, getting the job done in a replay.

Highlights were many, include Euxton Villa hitting Atherton LR for six without reply, South Liverpool edging out Ramsbottom United 4-2 in a back-and-forth thriller, and Nelson taking one step closer to big Wembley from Little Wembley, outdoing Stockport Georgians in a 3-2 win.

2. The Edward Case Cup is here!

This past weekend didn't just see the return of the FA Cup, but also, the Edward Case! The NWCFL's ol' reliable First Division Trophy saw a few interesting scorelines be recorded in Saturday's Preliminary Round.

By far the most eye-popping was Fulwood Amateurs 8-2 demolition of tournament debutants Halewood Apollo at Lightfoot Green Lane. But they weren't the only big winners - Flixton and Maine Road also scored four without reply against Ashton Athletic and AFC Blackpool respectively.

3. Droylsden's 12th man returns

After Saturday's FA Cup EP round finished as a tie at Burscough's Community Ground for visiting Droylsden, their replay fixture that took place on Tuesday emanated from their Butchers Arms stadium. Now that they have played their first two competitive home games of the season, their next will see the return of their fans!

After some unsavoury scenes following their play-off final victory on home soil against Maghull in the First Division North last season, Droylsden were ordered to play their first two competitive home games of the new campaign behind closed doors. Following Tuesday's 3-0 replay victory over the Linnets, and ahead of next Tuesday's home fixture against FC Isle of Man, those doors will be opened once more.

4. Nobody's perfect in the North

The campaign is only two weeks old, and we might already have all the evidence in front of us for a tense and unpredictable season of football in the First Division North. Already, every perfect record that previously existed in the division has been extinguished.

As of the time of writing, joint leaders Maghull and Holker Old Boys have one each in the loss column, with all the unbeaten teams remaining (Woolton, Daisy Hill, Ashton Athletic and, interestingly, 13th placed Darwen FC) having a tally in their draw column. If anyone can beat anyone, we might be in for a topsy-turvy season.

5. Flixton the place to be for thrillers

Flixton already bagged plenty of headlines with their re-emergence into semi-pro football before the season started, and now they're bagging even more by virtue of the sheer number of goals that seem to be scored in every game they play.

Since their opening day 1-1 draw against Squires Gate, the Valley Road side haven't featured in a game where one side has failed to score at least four. They shipped so many against Cammell Laird 1907 in a 4-3 defeat; scored so many in a 4-0 clean sheet against Ashton Athletic in the ECC, and went one better in a 5-2 win against Halewood Apollo in midweek.

articles.title: Week 2: Manager Quotes
articles.meta: Mon 10th August 2026 | Manager Reactions | By Media Team
articles.body:
Emirates FA Cup:

Euxton Villa made their own piece of history with their win this weekend in the FA Cup. They smashed Atherton LR for six without reply, after which manager Matty Atherton said, "it's an historic day for the club yesterday as we played our first ever fixture at home in the FA Cup. Lots of effort off the field to ensure we were in the best place possible, but I don’t think any of us anticipated what would happen on the field!

"An unbelievable 6-0 victory which has to rank right near the top of our most memorable victories since moving into the semi-professional ranks. Huge credit has to be given to the players who were relentless from the first whistle to the last on what was a very hot day to play football.

"We couldn’t have asked for more from them as they were quicker, sharper and hungrier than their opposite numbers, which led to a comfortable victory in the end. We know what a good side Atherton LR are through our many bottles that we’ve had over recent seasons.

"There’s a lot to admire about how they’ve continued to progress since moving into the Prem at the same time as us, and I am sure they will be right up there come the end of the season.

"But the result today was very much one for the Villa faithful to savour and means we go into uncharted territory for the next round of the FA Cup against Lower Breck in two weeks time - we can’t wait!"

Another NWCFL Premier Division side who progressed in English football's oldest competition were Litherland REMYCA. They overcame Charnock Richard 2-1, having lost to them in midweek. Following the game, manager Ste Scott said, "it was the perfect fixture for us after the disappointment of midweek. We approached the game today with a lot more intent and felt we were good value for the lead.

"The game got a bit edgy towards the end as you’d expect from a close cup tie, but all in all, we felt like we earned the win, just as Charnock had against us in the league midweek."

Longridge Town were also able to secure their spot in the next round. They eeked out a 1-0 victory away from home against Northern Counties East League side Keighley Town, which manager Lee Ashcroft called a "close game on a difficult pitch", but told of how he was "very happy to see out the victory".

Edward Case Cup:

There was a 10-goal thriller on Saturday amongst the opening fixtures of this year's Edward Case Cup. In the north draw, Fulwood Amateurs ran out 8-2 winners against new arrivals Halewood Apollo. Following such an impressive victory, manager Phil Blackwell said, "it was really pleasing to win our first home game of the season and obviously we're very happy with the result.

"We scored some late goals, which meant the final scoreline flattered us really. Halewood Apollo are going to be a really strong side this season. They have some real quality, and some experienced players. They obviously rested a few players but we wanted to try and keep the momentum from a solid start to the season for us so far, so we are really happy we managed to do that and progress to the next round."

Also victorious in the ECC north draw were Colne, who were away from home on Saturday to face Garstang. Gaffer Andy Harrison was not present as his side won 3-0, but did was still keen to speak about the preparation his team had managed.

"I wasn't at the game, but we prepared really well during the week after a tough opener. Training was superb and the lads were keen to bounce back. Alex and Marco took the team yesterday, so all credit to them for what was a fantastic performance and result. We've got a big game coming on Tuesday to hopefully kick start the league campaign."

Flixton are also in the next round after a 4-0 win over Ashton Athletic. Manager Alex Mortimer said "I am really happy with the performance and result against a good side who have started the season really well.

"The lads are starting to form relationships now and hopefully that result will kick us on as we go into Tuesday's home game with Halewood Apollo full of confidence."

First Division North:

In the North, Maghull broke Holker Old Boys' perfect start to the league season with a dominant 4-1 win on home soil. After full time, manager Joe Burns said, "it was a slow start for us today.

"We got to grips with the game mid-way through the first half, and totally dominated second half. The lads were fantastic throughout, and totally deserved to win - honestly, it could have been more in the end!"

Fans of Thornton Cleveleys would've been forgiven for leaving their away game against Ashton Town early. With 10 minutes to go, they were 2-0 down, but they turned it around for a mightily impressive 3-2 win.

Following the whistle, gaffer Paul Gregory said, "we didn't turn up for the first 80 minutes, but we got a goal from a long throw and it spurred us into life.

"We really kicked on for the last 10 minutes and we're delighted that we got the result - we arent at our best yet!"

First Division South:

Telford Town registered their first win of the season on Saturday with a 3-2 win over Alsager Town. Manager Shaun Ralph was in high spirits afterwards saying "Today’s first half was the best team performance we have produced to date, and credit must go to the whole group. Our new signings played a big part in helping us establish a two-goal lead going into half-time.

"Unfortunately, our standards dropped in the second half, allowing Alsager back into the game and bringing them level. With that in mind, we brought on a few players who have the ability to change a game, and one of those was George Dawes. His desire to drive at defenders was evident as he picked up the ball on the left, drove forward and smashed home the winner from 20 yards! A fantastic finish and a huge moment for George and the team.

"Full credit to the lads for digging deep and getting the win. Onto the next one!"

Barnton also secured their first win with a comeback victory at last seasons runners up Eccleshall. Manager Lewis Wood said afterwards "What a massive result for us as a group, both on and off the pitch. Those first three points are finally on the board!

"It was a fantastic win against a very good Eccleshall side, and hopefully this gives everyone the confidence and belief to kick on from here. Now we have to build on it!"

Finally New Miills made it two wins at Church Lane from two with a last gasp 2-1 win over Allscott Heath. One half of their Management team spoke to us afterwads saying "After Tuesdays performance it was all about a bounce back from us and getting back on track. The lads know we have to make Church Lane a difficult place to come and they all put a great shift in.

"Changes were made from midweek and a fresh Luc Ferry caused havoc down the wing all game whilst Marcello coming in for his first start of the season was an absolute rock at the back. We needed 3 points no matter what, and we achieved that.

"The fans played their part as always, they were fantastic and created a great atmosphere cheering the lads to a win Now focus turns to another tough away trip to Sandbach on Tuesday."

articles.title: Wythenshawe win the 2026 NWCFL Champions Cup!
articles.meta: Mon 27th July 2026 | Announcements | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
The NWCFL Premier Division Champions for 2025/26, Wythenshawe, won the league's annual Champions Cup 3-0 in a cagey game against defending Macron Cup champions AFC Liverpool on Saturday.

James Kinsey's men have been hard at work throughout pre-season, preparing for a return to the Northern Premier League in 2026/27, but their business in the NWCFL had not yet finished before last weekend's meeting with a new-look AFC Liverpool side.

The visitors to the Avensure Community Stadium have undergone a radical transformation since lifting the Macron Cup in early May. Long-time manager Phil Stafford departed for league rivals Burscough, and several players have also left for newer pastures. Regardless, new gaffer Jack Edwards led a determined side into this curtain-jerker.

The game itself started exactly the way that the Ammies wanted, with George Sankey rising the highest to turn home an Eoin Charles cross from close range after just eight minutes.

Being forced onto the back foot so early seemed to wake something up inside AFC Liverpool, who began to find answers to everything the hosts were throwing at them for the next half hour of play. On top of that, they were able to work a few chances of their own into the mix and scared the Wythenshawe back line a handful of times.

AFC would be undone again, however, with eight minutes to go before half time. Prince Chidera danced into the penalty area from the left before falling over an outstretched leg, and the referee wasted no time pointing to the spot. Aaron Dwyer stepped up from 12 yards and made no mistake, firing high down the middle as AFC goalkeeper and skipper Harry Campbell dived to his right.

The second half was not one for the history books from a neutral perspective, but it was exactly what the hosts, leading 2-0, were hoping for. There was very little for either side to cheer about in the first 25 minutes of the second period, but on 72 minutes, Wythy put the ball in the AFC net for a third time from close range, only for the assistant referee's flag to curtail the celebrations.

Another 20 minutes of half chances and solid defensive work from both teams came and went, before the fourth official's board went up to indicate stoppage time. Before the full-time whistle, there would be one more pivotal moment.

AFC Liverpool failed to conclusively clear their lines after a long ball over the top for Wythenshawe, and it looked for all the world like goalkeeper Campbell had handled outside of the box. The referee let Wythy have the advantage, since they still held possession, and Joel Ankers found Sandro Da Costa on the edge of the box who rifled a strike in off the crossbar to seal a 3-0 win.

Following the game, and the trophy lift, victorious manager James Kinsey said, "I thought they (AFC Liverpool) were the better team in the first 10-15 minutes. They had more energy and they were on the front foot. But once we got going and got onto the front foot, it became a possession based game and I thought we gained full control. At half time, we spoke about retaining the ball when we had it, and the spectators might not have enjoyed it because we killed the game a bit, but as a manager, I'm buzzing that we were so dominant. Another trophy for the cabinet, and we're really happy."

Looking back on what had been an excellent league season in the NWCFL in 2025/26, James said, "the first four of five months weren't great, but after that point, we started to really enjoy ourselves. We've got a really good, young, hungry group of lads at this club. They're determined; they have a point to prove every time they play, and that mentality was important for our recruitment this summer - we didn't need to reinvent the wheel.

"Our group from last season is more than capable of competing at the level above, and we've kept 99% of that group together. So, we're really, really excited for the new season. We know it will be really difficult, but when you look around the ground and at the facilities? This club is going places.

Looking ahead to the NPL in 2026/27, James said, "We're wanting to stay up next season. Personally, I'd love to say, 'we're going to win the league', but as a club, we need to solidify ourselves as an NPL club. We'll be going out to win every game, and internally, we want to compete for something come the end of the season. But if we stay up, it will be a remarkable season for us - the club has never had more than one season at that level. We need to get there so we can become established.

"We've got to respect the level we're going into - some of the other clubs have more finances, more infrastructure than we have, but we are catching up. Hospitality upgrades, a new stand - it's really exciting to be at this club at this time. We've just got to be patient on the pitch and enjoy these times we're having."

Congratulations to everyone at Wythenshawe, and we wish them the best of luck in the NPL. We also wish the best of luck to runners-up AFC Liverpool, in the NWCFL Premier Division.

articles.title: Introducing the new member clubs: Halewood Apollo
articles.meta: Tue 28th July 2026 | Halewood Apollo | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
With the 2026/27 NWCFL campaign fast approaching, now is the perfect time to introduce the new member clubs to their respective divisions.

Or perhaps better – to let the new member clubs introduce themselves.

Last week, I spoke to Joseph Stocks – owner, chairman and first team manager at Halewood Apollo, who will take their place in the NWCFL First Division North this season following promotion from the Liverpool County Premier League after the end of the 2025/26 season.

It has been nothing shy of a whirlwind decade plus for Halewood Apollo Football Club.

They were founded in 2014 by reigning chairman Joseph Stocks, and they began their competitive life in Division Five of the Warrington & District League, purely as an enthusiastic friend group with a passion for the beautiful game.

Five promotions in their local league would follow, several of which came back-to-back, and by the turn of the decade, Halewood Apollo were sitting at the top table in the pyramid – the Warrington & District League Premier Division.

In the club’s final season before making the next step, they had an excellent run to the Liverpool County FA Challenge Cup semi-finals, competing against well-established and historic Liverpool-based teams along the way.

Playing against the best amateur players that the city had to offer would become commonplace for Apollo as of 2020, when they were promoted to the Liverpool County Premier League pyramid.

Their first season in the Liverpool County Prem saw them secure promotion from Division One to the Premier Division after a fourth placed finish, and they would become accustomed to sitting at the top table within their home county league during the next five seasons.

The club finished eighth in their debut Prem season, but it would be their second campaign that would see them establish themselves as title challengers. They finished as runners-up in 2022/23, behind current NWCFL side and local rivals Woolton (still with their MSB prefix attached). However, they wouldn’t have to wait much longer to put their own names on the trophy.

They were crowned league champions the very next season, in 2023/24. They pipped East Villa Rail to the title by a mere point to lift the league trophy, but Apollo were unable to reap the rewards of promotion at that time due to their facilities not meeting the criteria for a Step Six club.

As a fix to this problem, the club developed a close working relationship with Knowsley Council to transform their home facilities at Halewood Leisure Centre and deliver significant ground improvements to meet Step Six requirements. Included in these improvements were new seated and covered standing accommodation, additional spectator facilities, and outdoor toilets, amongst other infrastructure.

Despite failing to defend their league title in 2024/25 and dropping as low as eighth (again) in the division, they fought their way back into promotion contention in 2025/26. Apollo snuck into fifth place in the table ahead of Waterloo Dock by just a point, despite a less than desirable goal difference of -16.

A top five finish was enough to allow their application for promotion to be taken considered. Given the improvements made to their facilities since the last time a Step Six berth was made possible by their league standing, they were accepted into the NWCFL First Division North ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

----------

Joseph Stocks

1. How would you describe Halewood Apollo to someone who had never heard of the club?

a. Halewood Apollo is a community club based in the very south of Liverpool. We won the Liverpool County Premier League in 2024, and we have grown rapidly over the last decade.

We're much more than just a football club – we're at the heart of our community, with a thriving junior section, a first team now competing in the North West Counties League, and a real ambition to keep growing both on and off the pitch.

2. What does the club mean to the area and community that you can represent?

a. We're a genuine community club, and that is something we're incredibly proud of. We have a junior section with over 40 teams, providing opportunities for hundreds of local children every week. Alongside that, through Apollo Active, we deliver free sport, education and health programmes for young people across the area.

We want people to see Halewood Apollo as a club that genuinely cares about its community, and I think you can feel that when you come to our games. It's becoming much more than just 90 minutes of football.

3. Tell me about the manager.

a. That would be me!

I'm the proud founder of Halewood Apollo, having started the club back in 2014, and I've been involved in every step of the journey since day one. As the club continues to grow, my long-term ambition is to move into more of a board-level role, overseeing the direction and long-term development of Halewood Apollo both on and off the pitch.

Right now, though, my full focus is on managing the team and making sure we have a successful first season in the North West Counties Football League. It's a huge year for the club, and I'm fully committed to giving everything I can to help us establish ourselves at this level.

4. Tell me a bit about last season – your last one in the Liverpool County Premier League. Was promotion a definite goal, or a happy accident?

a. It's been a crazy few years for the club. In 2024 we won the Liverpool County Premier League with a squad that probably had enough quality to compete as high as Step Four. We already knew we were working with Knowsley Council to upgrade our facilities to reach Step Six, but unfortunately the groundworks weren't going to be finished in time.

As a result, we lost 17 players, many of whom moved higher up the pyramid, and we had to completely rebuild the squad. The following season we finished mid-table, which I honestly think was one of our biggest achievements considering everything that had happened.

Going into last season, we could see the ground improvements really starting to take shape, but we also knew we didn't have a squad capable of winning the league. Our aim was simply to finish in the top five and hope that one of the promotion places became available.

By December we were sitting around 10th, and promotion looked a long way off, but the lads showed unbelievable character. We added a few players, went on a brilliant run in the second half of the season and managed to sneak into the top five. To then secure promotion made all the hard work worthwhile.

5. How well have you been getting along with your pre-season prep? New signings, friendlies, etc?

a. When we were promoted, a lot of people questioned whether we'd be able to compete at Step Six after the previous couple of seasons. Personally, I always believed promotion was the best thing that could happen to the club. The standard of players available to us instantly improved, because a lot of players we wanted to work with simply didn't want to play below Step Six anymore.

We've brought in an almost completely new squad, with players arriving from higher divisions alongside several talented young lads from our outstanding under-18’s side, who won the Liverpool Premier League title last season.

Pre-season has gone really well. We've played six games, winning three and drawing three, and we finished with a fantastic 2-0 victor over Widnes Town, who have also just joined the NWCFL. The squad has gelled quickly and we're all looking forward to getting the league campaign underway.

6. What are your ambitions for the upcoming 2026/27 season in the NWCFL?

a. We never wanted to come into the North West Counties League with the minimum target being survival. We believe in what we've built at Halewood Apollo, and we believe we've assembled a squad capable of competing.

Our minimum target is to challenge for the play-offs. We know that's a big ask in a league with 22 strong teams, but we've always believed in setting ambitious goals. If we don't achieve that, I think everyone at the club will be disappointed because we genuinely believe we've got the quality to compete.

----------

We wish everyone at Halewood Apollo all the best for the 2026/27 season!

There is just one midweek round across both competitions this season - the 1st Round of the Edward Case Cup is penned in for week commencing 5th October 2026 and will be played 'under the lights'.

articles.title: Week 1: Preview
articles.meta: Sat 1st August 2026 | Match Previews | By Ben Wilkinson
articles.body:
The wait is over. After a summer of preparation, the NWCFL returns this Saturday with a full programme across the Premier Division, First Division North and First Division South. The opening day of the season is notoriously difficult to predict, particularly in a league as competitive as ours, but it offers plenty of intrigue as new signings, promoted sides and fresh ambitions look to get off to a dream start to the new campaign.

There are a number of fresh faces in this year's competition as no fewer than eleven clubs join us who weren't here last time out; some familiar faces and some brand new to the fold.

Premier Division

One of the standout fixtures of the day comes from Crilly Park. Atherton LR were among the Premier Division's strongest sides last season, making an instant impact following promotion last summer and plenty will be expecting them to challenge again. Their first opposition this term is in the form of newly promoted Nelson, who face a stern test immediately upon their own return to Step 5 and a positive result would send a message to the rest of the league that they aren’t just here to make up the numbers.

Droylsden's first bout at this level since the club re-activated after the pandemic is a home tie against Macron Cup winners AFC Liverpool at the Butchers' Arms. It's been a summer of change for the visiting Non-League Reds following their cup triumph and the Bloods will pose stiff opposition in their first league encounter since. Chadderton enter the campaign with hopes of another strong season after a 5th-placed finish in 2025/26 and their first fixture is away at stalwarts Charnock Richard, who didn't build on a strong season in 2024/25 and will be looking to right the wrongs of last season from the very start.

Things are looking bright at Burscough with many tipping the Linnets to do even better than their 10th place of last season. Standing in the way of them first up is a Prestwich Heys outfit who fell just short of the play-off places; expect a tight game at the Community Ground this afternoon.

Ramsbottom United begin the season as one of the promotion favourites after finishing runners-up last term, although Steve Wilkes' retirement from the dugout marks the dawn of a new era at the Harry Williams Riverside Stadium. First up for them is a trip to Litherland Sports Park to take on Litherland REMYCA. The Remy were repreived from relegation by the FA after finishing 23rd last season, a slight uptick in form towards the end of the campaign seeing them finish on 27 points from 46 games. They will be looking to put last season firmly in the rear-view mirror and hope to make maximum use of their good fortune in the close-season.

Trafford return to the NWCFL fold after 18 years in the NPL and Longridge Town are the first visitors to Shawe View. The Ridge have developed a bit of a reputation in recent seasons for being partial to a goal-fest, often with some huge margins of victory and defeat, so once again will be ones to watch for the neutrals.

The late kick off sees FC St Helens visit The Bowl in Douglas where they come up against FC Isle of Man at 6pm. The Ravens had a disappointing season in 2025/25, finishing 20th and recording their worst finish since promotion from the First Division South in 2021/22.

Other fixtures:

First Division North

It's a new-look First Division North for 2026/27 - the 18-team division of recent years being expanded to 22 clubs and as a result there are SIX new clubs in this division. Three of those have been promoted from County Feeder Leagues over the summer after successfully applying for and being granted promotion into the National League System.

All three of those clubs have been handed away fixtures on the opening day. AFC Knowsley get their longest trek of the season out of the way early doors as they head up to the Handmark Engineering Stadium where Holker Old Boys provide the opposition for their first game in the NWCFL. Holker are experienced heads at this level of the game and will provide an early yardstick for AFC Knowsley.

Uppermill make the journey east to Birkenhead to take on Ashville with both clubs being new to this division. Ashville have been laterally moved from the South division whilst Uppermill finished as runners-up in the Manchester League and play at this level for the very first time.

Also transferred in from the First Division South are another Wirral-based outfit in Cammell Laird 1907. Lairds had been in the Southern section since the First Division was split back in 2018 so will come up against plenty of new opposition, the first of which being Thornton Cleveleys, who are now in their third season at this level and after missing out on the play-offs by just two points last time out they will be coming out of the blocks firing.

Woolton, recently dropping their 'MSB' prefix for their first team, finished in an impressive 3rd position in their Counties debut last term and a trip to Colne provides their first opportunity to build on that strong foundation and aim for promotion in their sophomore year, whilst Colne will be looking to turn themselves around after a turbulent few years, tumbling from the NPL to 15th place in the North in 2025/26.

Halewood Apollo are another brand new side for the League and join us following a 5th-placed finish in the Liverpool County Premier League, a setup that has provided us with a number of success stories down the years. Apollo will be hoping to join that particular list in the coming years but first up for them is a trip to Garstang. The Stang have struggled in recent years and were handed a repreive for the third year in succession over the summer. Time will tell whether they can push back up the league table and leave fate in their own hands by the time the final whistle of the season blows.

Along with the promotions and lateral movements, there is one direct entrant to the division from outside of the pyramid and the name may well ring a few bells for those who have been in the game for a short while: Flixton. The original club were in the NWCFL between 1986 and 2012, barring a four-year stint in the NPL in the late 90s. They left the League following the conclusion of the 2011/12 season following a period of decline but have been revived under new ownership and were accepted into Step 6 for the 2026/27 season. Their first competitive fixture in 14 years comes in the form of an away trip to Squires Gate, who will not stand for just being part of the occasion.

Other fixtures:

First Division South

It's all change too in the First Division South, with five clubs waving their goodbyes and SEVEN coming in to replace them! Like in the North, there are three clubs joining us from County Feeder Leagues, with a couple of what now appears to be usual transfers in from the Midland League and another new club.

AFC Bridgnorth, transferred from the Midland League, begin life in the NWCFL looking to make an immediate statement at their Crown Meadow home. However, Foley Meir are unlikely to make things easy for them as they build on a solid 11th place finish last term.

We welcome Dawley Town into the National League System after their superb season in the Shropshire County League, culminating in the championship and a successful promotion application. Their first task in the NWCFL is to get the better of a stubborn Alsager Town side at Wood Park on Saturday afternoon.

Market Drayton Town were granted a reprieve from relegation and their stay of execution begins with a home game against new boys Brereton Social, champions of the Staffordshire County League in the spring and arriving into the Counties with bags of momentum and will therefore provide Market Drayton with a very tough test as the hosts look to put some points on the board at the first opportunity.

Also coming to us from the Midland League Division One are Bilston Town, who come up against a familiar face in gameweek 1 as they face off against Shawbury United for the first time in the league since they were both in the Midland League back in 2023/24.

The third side to be given the sidways move is Wednesfield Community, who arrive into the NWCFL fold off the back of two successive second-bottom finishes in the Midland League Division One. They will be hoping that a change of scenery equates to a change of results on the pitch but they will need to be at their very best to get the victory over Sandbach United, who are now in their 11th season at this level and impressively have never finished below 8th!

Other fixtures:

articles.title: Week 1: Summary
articles.meta: Sat 1st August 2026 | Match Reviews | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
PREMIER DIVISION

Burscough were the big winners on the opening day of the 2026/27 season in the Premier Division after a 4-1 win over Prestwich Heys. Joel Skillen scored twice for the home side there with both of his goals coming in stoppage time.

Trafford also impressed on their return to the NWCFL after relegation last season with a 3-0 win at home to Longridge Town in front of an impressive crowd of 362.

Glossop North End ran out 2-0 winners at home to Euxton Villa with Droylsden's first game in the Premier Division ending in a 1-0 win over AFC Liverpool. Nelson also won on their return with a 2-1 win at Atherton LR, their winner coming in stoppage time.

Abbey Hey drew 2-2 with Barnoldswick Town thanks to Callum Pugh's 90th minute penalty, with Charnock Richard drawing 1-1 with Chadderton. There was also a 1-1 draw at South Liverpool against Irlam, the visitors levelling in stoppage time there, whilst Litherland REMYCA and Ramsbottom United also played out the same scoreline.

FC Isle of Man play the final game of the day at 18:00 at home to FC St Helens.

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

It was a superb opening day of the season for Daisy Hill who ran out 5-0 winners at home to Steeton. Gerald-Junior McCullion and William Shawcross both scored twice for the Westhoughton side in their biggest opening day win.

There were seven goals in Cumbria as Holker Old Boys ran out 4-3 winners against AFC Knowsley. There were three equalisers in that game, before Patrick Allington hit the winner for Holker three minutes into stoppage time.

Thornton Cleveleys came from two goals down to win 3-2 at home to Cammell Laird 1907, with Kyle Higham hitting a late winner. Woolton were impressive 3-1 winners at Colne.

Bacup Borough were impressive 3-0 winners at home to Ashton Town, with Halewood Apollo getting a win on debut as they won 3-1 at Garstang.

Darwen came from behind to win 2-1 at home to Maghull thanks to Sam Holt's late goal, that in front of the divisions biggest crowd of 279, with Ashton Athletic winning 2-0 at home to AFC Blackpool thanks to Josh Nicholson's late double.

Squires Gate and Flixton played out a 1-1 draw with Maine Road drawing with Fulwood Amateurs by the same scoreline.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

New Mills are the early leaders in the South as they won 6-0 at home to Telford Town, with Solomon Richards and Luke Evans both scoring twice.

Wolverhampton Casuals won 3-0 at newly promoted Crewe with Kieran Cook scoring twice, whilst it was a good day for AFC Bridgnorth in their debut game with Suar Dedja scoring twice in a 3-1 win over Foley Meir.

Bilston Town also won on debut, 2-0 at home to Shawbury United, with fellow new-boys Brereton Social matching their scoreline with victory at Market Drayton Town.

Last seasons runners up Eccleshall started this campaign with a 3-1 win at home to Widnes Town, with Joe Bevan grabbing a brace as Sandbach United beat Wednesfield Community 2-1.

Barnton scored the first goal of the new season in just the second minute of their game through Jordan Sherlock, but visitors Stafford Town hit back to win 2-1.

The final two games both ended 2-2. Dawley Town looked to be heading to defeat on debut when Alsager Town made it 2-0 with four minutes remaining, however a Ross Jones penalty and an own goal gave them a point. The final game saw Cheadle Heath Nomads come from two down to draw at Allscott Heath.
